title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, how-tos, roadmap, team wiki
author: Hannah Garcia
content:
Overview

This consolidated platform engineering reference covers our systems & services inventory, common how-tos, recommended dashboards and alerting rules, core runbooks for oncall and incident response, the platform roadmap for the next three quarters, and pointers to the team wiki. The document is intended as the single source of operational truth for the Platform team and SREs.

Goals
- Provide clear ownership and SLIs/SLOs for each platform service.
- Standardize alerts to reduce noise and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA).
- Supply reproducible runbooks for common incidents and maintenance tasks.
- Surface roadmap priorities tied to reliability and cost-efficiency.

Audience and scope
- Primary: Platform engineers, oncall SREs, Platform product managers.
- Secondary: Eng infra, Serving runtime, Security, and Customer Success.
- Scope: services owned by eng-platform (dashboards, service mesh, routing, autoscaling, monitoring, runbooks, observability). Does not duplicate service-level design docs found in eng-serving-runtime.

Systems & services inventory (high level)
- platform-controlplane (k8s control plane for platform services) — owner: platform-controlplane@redwood.com — SLO: 99.95% control plane API availability.
- routing-gateway (edge API proxy / Kong/Gloo) — owner: platform-networking — SLO: 99.9% request success for internal service-to-service traffic.
- telemetry-ingest (Prometheus remote_write / Cortex) — owner: platform-metrics — SLO: 99.9% write availability, max scrape latency 30s.
- alert-manager (Alertmanager + PD integration) — owner: platform-observability — SLO: 99.9% delivery to PagerDuty.
- autoscaler (KEDA + custom scaler) — owner: platform-scaling — SLO: scale-to-target within 90s for CPU-based scaling, 120s for queue-based scaling.
- dashboard-store (Grafana + dashboards repo) — owner: platform-observability — SLO: dashboards load <2s 95th percentile.
- shared-cache (redis cluster for prefix/KV caching) — owner: platform-cache — SLO: 99.95% availability, p95 latency <5ms.

How-tos (common procedures)
1) Adding a new Grafana dashboard
   - Create dashboard JSON in dashboards/ directory in the repo. Follow the naming convention: team-service-metric-dashboard.json
   - Run `make grafana-import` (CI job) to validate schema and import into staging Grafana.
   - Assign dashboard owner in dashboard metadata and add to team wiki.
   - Rollout to prod via `./scripts/promote-dashboard --id <staging-id>` after review.

2) Adding a service to alerting
   - Create an alert rule in prometheus/rules/<service>-alerts.yml. Use standardized labels: severity, team, owner, pagerduty_service.
   - Alerts must include a 5-minute and 30-minute evaluation window. Prefer composite alerts over 1-off flapping thresholds.
   - Submit PR and request review from platform-observability. On merge, ensure index names are present in Alertmanager routing.

3) Oncall pre-shift checklist (10m)
   - Confirm PagerDuty rotation and escalation for your shift.
   - Open primary dashboards (Platform Overview, Control Plane, Telemetry Ingest, GPU Queue).
   - Check any active maintenance windows.
   - Run `kubectl get nodes` and `kubectl get pods -n platform` to confirm steady state.

Dashboards & alerts (recommended panels and rules)
- Platform Overview (Grafana folder: Platform / Overview) 
  - Panels: API request rate (RPS), p50/p95/p99 latency for platform gateway, error rate (5m), control plane errors, infra CPU/GPU utilization, cluster autoscaler events.
  - Queries: PromQL examples included in Appendix.

- Telemetry Ingest dashboard
  - Panels: remote_write success rate, ingestion lag (seconds), compaction backlog, Prometheus TSDB head block size, Cortex ingester series count.

- GPU Fleet dashboard
  - Panels: GPU utilization by server, queued jobs, average token throughput, GPU memory pressure, drain events.
  - Alert: gpu_queue_length > 50 for 5m -> severity: high -> page platform-scaling.

Examples of high-value alerts (templates)
- Platform gateway: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-gateway",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-gateway"}[5m])) > 0.01` -> page platform-oncall if sustained 3m.
- Control plane: `apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="kube-apiserver"}` p99 > 1s for 5m -> page platform-controlplane.
- Telemetry ingest: `increase(prometheus_remote_write_failures_total[5m]) > 0` -> page platform-observability.
- Shared-cache latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redis_command_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.005` -> severity: medium.

Alert routing and escalation
- Alertmanager routes by `pagerduty_service` label. Use dedicated PD services for: platform-oncall, platform-scaling, platform-observability, platform-networking.
- Escalation policy: 0-15m primary oncall -> 15-45m secondary -> 45+ exec rotation.
- All alerts that page the oncall must include runbook_url and useful diagnostics (examples provided below). Alerts without runbook_url will be rejected in PR review.

Platform runbooks (primary runbooks summarized)
1) Control plane degraded (apiserver high latency / ETCD unavailable)
   - Symptoms: kubectl commands time out, apiserver p99 > 1s, etcd leader change messages.
   - Immediate actions (0-5m):
     1. Notify oncall and declare incident in incident channel #platform-incidents.
     2. Run `kubectl get --raw=/healthz` and `kubectl get componentstatuses`.
     3. Check etcd cluster health: `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=<endpoints> endpoint status` and `etcdctl endpoint health`.
   - Remediation (5-30m):
     1. If an etcd member is unhealthy, cordon and restart the node (document node ID).
     2. If control plane pods are OOM, increase requests temporarily and restart pod.
   - Rollback and verification (30-60m):
     1. Validate API responsiveness with `kubectl get nodes` and platform overview dashboard.
     2. Postmortem: capture timeline, root cause, and action items.

2) Telemetry ingest backlog
   - Symptoms: ingestion lag > 120s, remote_write failures, rising storage churn.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Pause non-critical scrapes (switch prometheus config to reduced job set).
     2. Increase ingester replicas: `kubectl scale deployment/cortex-ingester --replicas=N+2`.
     3. Open a maintenance window if capacity scaling will cause transient alerts.

3) GPU queue overflow (tokens slowed, model serving degraded)
   - Symptoms: queued requests > 50, p99 latency for generation spikes, autoscaler not reacting.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Page platform-scaling.
     2. Check GPU host health and driver errors: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` on hosts.
     3. If safe, increase burst pool by promoting reserved capacity: `./scripts/promote-burst --pool <pool-name>`

Runbook hygiene and ownership
- Every runbook must have a named owner, last-tested date, and post-incident verification steps.
- Runbooks are stored in docs/runbooks/ in the platform repo and must include a short playbook summary in the dashboard panel for the related alert.

Retrospectives and postmortems
- Template: timeline, impact (customers/latency/cost), root cause analysis, detection timeline, mitigation steps, action items with owners and due dates, regression risk, and verification plan.
- Conduct a blameless retrospective for any incident with Sev >= high or availability impact > 30 minutes.
- Maintain an action-item tracker (label: platform-pmo) and surface recurring issues to roadmap planning.

Platform roadmap (Q1–Q3 2027, prioritized)
- Q1 2027: Observability hardening
  - Roll out tenant-aware metrics ingestion to reduce cross-tenant noisy neighbors.
  - Migrate Alertmanager to HA 3-node cluster.
  - Replace legacy Grafana panels with standardized templates and lifecycle tests.
- Q2 2027: Autoscaling & cost optimization
  - Implement predictive scaling for GPU pools (ML-based forecast).
  - Introduce smarter batching/caching profiles for common model families.
  - Start pilot of quantization-aware routing to reduce cost for embedding workloads.
- Q3 2027: Private deployment & compliance readiness
  - Harden private VPC deployment automation for on-prem customers.
  - Add audit-log replay tooling to support compliance evidence collection.
  - Performance tests for 99.95% availability under regional failover.

Team wiki & ownership
- Team wiki is the single index for ephemeral notes, meeting artifacts, and link-outs. Key wiki pages: oncall-rotations, runbook-testing-calendar, dashboards-change-log, and playbook-retrospectives.
- Owners must keep the `last-tested` date up to date on the wiki when they execute a runbook during an incident or drill.

Appendix: example PromQL and alert rule snippets
- PromQL: p99 latency for routing gateway  `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="routing-gateway"}[5m])) by (le))`
- Alert rule YAML (example):
  ```yaml
  groups:
  - name: routing-gateway.rules
    rules:
    - alert: RoutingGatewayErrorRate
      expr: |
        sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-gateway",status!~"2.."}[5m]))
        / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-gateway"}[5m])) > 0.01
      for: 3m
      labels:
        severity: high
        team: platform-networking
        pagerduty_service: platform-oncall
      annotations:
        summary: "High error rate on routing-gateway"
        runbook_url: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/routing-gateway-error-rate"
  ```

Runbook testing cadence
- Quarterly tabletop exercises for each critical runbook.
- Annual full-scale game day for control plane and telemetry ingest.

Ownership and next steps
- Owners: platform-observability (dashboards, alerts), platform-controlplane (k8s), platform-scaling (autoscaler/GPU pools), platform-cache (redis), platform-networking (gateway).
- Next steps: owners to review this doc in the next 2 weeks, confirm SLOs, and add explicit runbook links for each alert.
